newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco supervisors okay extra library funds.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco supervisors okay extra library funds.

text.p: San Francisco supervisors have taken steps to seize fiscal control of the public library system, approving a $1.6 million funding package to ease the system's deficit, officials said on Thursday.
The Board of Supervisors' budget committee told library officials that their fiscal management of the system would be closely audited.
In addition, the mayor's budget director and the city's controller were tapped to oversee the chief librarian's activities on a day-to-day basis.
The supplemental appropriation for the public library system followed the release of a critical report on library management by San Francisco Budget Analyst Harvey Rose.

Even with this assistance, the library was expected to be short nearly $1.3 million this year after overextending itself on salaries, overtime and benefits, Rose said in a letter to the budget committee.
